context.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system for a mid-size payment processor that evaluates card-not-present transactions for fraud, and provides case management for analysts. It operates within AWS eu-west-1 with strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, sub-50ms P99 latency, and a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Key Elements
* Payment Gateway / Processing Engine (External Actor): Submits authorization requests.
* Fraud Analyst / Risk Manager (External Actors): Perform case reviews and update fraud rules.
* Identity Provider (External System): Manages OIDC/OAuth2 authentication and MFA.
* Payment Card Network / Tokenization Vault (External System): Provides tokenized card data.
* Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (AWS Software System): Core scoring and case management platform.
* Secure Audit Archive (External System): Cold storage for tamper-evident retention.

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway to Fraud Screening System: Submits card-not-present authorizations via gRPC over TLS (mTLS) for sub-50ms scoring.
* Fraud Analysts to Fraud Screening System: Interacts via HTTPS (Web UI) protected by OIDC/OAuth2 for case management and rule updates.
* Fraud Screening System to Tokenization Vault: Resolves payment tokens via mTLS/HTTPS to enforce PCI-DSS scope reduction.
* Fraud Screening System to Secure Audit Archive: Writes decisions, model versions, and inputs via AWS SDK/S3 API using S3 Object Lock.
* Fraud Analysts/Risk Managers to Identity Provider: Authenticates via OIDC/OAuth2 over HTTPS with mandatory MFA.

## Technology Stack
* AWS Fargate on ARM64 (Graviton): Runs containerized workloads to optimize performance-per-dollar and maintain the 25,000 EUR budget.
* AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB): Handles gRPC traffic routing with strict health checks and automated 1-minute fail-open caching.
* AWS KMS: Cryptographically signs fallback tokens using short-lived asymmetric keys to prevent replay attacks during outages.
* AWS S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode): Ensures tamper-evident 7-year auditability of decisions, model versions, and inputs.
* AWS CloudWatch & Managed Prometheus/Grafana: Provides distributed tracing (X-Ray) and metrics without self-hosted operational overhead.

## Rationale
The architecture prioritizes a managed AWS serverless/container approach (Fargate, S3, KMS) to support a 3-engineer team within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Using gRPC/mTLS, AWS NLB, and cryptographic fallback caches satisfies sub-50ms P99 latency and 1-minute fail-open availability requirements while strictly maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud prior to approval and provides a case management interface for fraud analysts. It guarantees sub-50ms P99 decision latency at 3,000 transactions per second while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year audit trail.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst / Risk Manager, Merchant Operations Manager, Compliance Officer
- Payment Gateway / Processing Engine, Identity Provider, Payment Card Network / Tokenization Vault, Secure Audit Archive
- API Gateway (Nginx / AWS ALB)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Java/Quarkus or Go with embedded ONNX Runtime)
- Case Management Service (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Audit & Compliance Ledger (Rust or Go with AWS KMS-backed signing)
- Analytics Export Stream (Fluent Bit sidecar)
- Data Store (AWS Aurora PostgreSQL & Amazon Redis)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to API Gateway via HTTPS (REST/JSON)
- API Gateway to Fraud Scoring Engine via gRPC over internal ALB with mTLS
- Fraud Scoring Engine to Redis via TCP (TLS) for feature lookup
- Case Management Service to Identity Provider via OAuth2/OIDC over HTTPS
- Audit & Compliance Ledger to AWS S3 / Glacier via HTTPS (TLS)
- Fluent Bit sidecar to Amazon Athena/S3 via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on AWS Fargate: Compute platform for lightweight container deployment within the 25,000 EUR/month budget
- Java/Quarkus or Go with ONNX Runtime: Core scoring engine technology to guarantee sub-50ms P99 latency
- AWS KMS: Asymmetric key generation for cryptographic non-repudiation and tamper-evident audit logging
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & Redis: Relational storage for cases/audit and in-memory storage for low-latency feature stores
- Fluent Bit: Lightweight sidecar for scrubbing PII and streaming anonymized metrics

## Rationale
The architecture combines serverless AWS Fargate containers with low-latency Go/Quarkus runtimes to meet the strict 3,000 TPS and 50ms P99 performance requirements within a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Security isolations, mTLS, and AWS KMS-backed signing ensure strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates payment authorizations and manages suspicious transactions. Its core purpose is to prevent fraud, enforce PCI-DSS compliance, and provide low-latency risk decisions.]

## Key Elements
* Payment Gateway / Processing Engine
* API Gateway (AWS Regional ALB with AWS WAF)
* Envoy Proxy Sidecar
* Fraud Scoring Engine
* Tokenization Vault
* Amazon Redis
* Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway / Processing Engine -> API Gateway: Submits payment authorizations via HTTPS (REST/JSON)
* API Gateway -> Tokenization Vault: Sanitizes PANs and retrieves payment tokens via HTTPS (REST/JSON)
* API Gateway -> Envoy Proxy Sidecar: Routes sanitized requests via internal VPC Link
* Envoy Proxy Sidecar -> Fraud Scoring Engine: Forwards payloads via gRPC over TLS (mTLS)
* API Gateway -> Amazon Redis: Evaluates sliding-window rate limits via Redis protocol

## Technology Stack
* AWS ALB & AWS WAF: Managed edge security and rate limiting to prevent card-testing attacks within budget
* Amazon Redis: Low-latency distributed cache supporting high-throughput sliding-window rate limiting
* gRPC over TLS (mTLS): High-performance internal communication protocol guaranteeing sub-50ms P99 latency
* AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Private CA: Automated certificate lifecycle management for strict mTLS compliance

## Rationale
[This architecture uses AWS managed edge services and gRPC to meet the strict sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS under a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Edge tokenization and zero-logging ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while operating with a three-engineer team.]

Fraud Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud prior to approval, while providing a case management interface for fraud analysts. It is designed to process 3,000 requests per second with strict latency, security, and auditability constraints.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst / Risk Manager (User)
- API Gateway (Nginx / AWS ALB)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Java / Quarkus with embedded ONNX Runtime)
- Case Management Service (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Audit & Compliance Ledger (Rust / Go with AWS KMS-backed signing)
- Data Store (AWS Aurora PostgreSQL & Amazon Redis)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Fraud Scoring Engine: Forwards scoring requests via gRPC over TLS (mTLS)
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Amazon Redis: Performs feature lookups via TCP (TLS)
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Audit & Compliance Ledger: Emits signed audit payloads via gRPC
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Case Management Service: Feeds review decisions and risk factor summaries via internal event streams

## Technology Stack
- Java / Quarkus: Chosen for build-time optimization and low memory footprint to meet sub-50ms latency
- ONNX Runtime: Embedded locally in the scoring engine to execute models without network hops
- AWS ECS (Fargate): Provides cost-effective container orchestration within budget without Kubernetes overhead
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & Redis: Provides relational persistence and low-latency feature caching

## Rationale
This architecture uses an embedded inference engine and lightweight container orchestration to meet strict performance and budget constraints. Distributed services are minimized to guarantee predictable sub-50ms P99 latencies while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.

Case Management Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Service is a secure Node.js and TypeScript container that enables fraud analysts to review suspicious payment authorizations, execute bulk overrides, and submit rule feedback. It ensures strict PCI-DSS compliance and operational auditability without exposing raw card data.

## Key Elements
* Case API Controller (Node.js/Express)
* Case Business Logic & Orchestration Service (including Bulk Operation Processor)
* Card Masking / Tokenizer Integration Client
* Audit & Immutable Ledger Publisher
* Rule Feedback Publisher
* AWS Fargate, AWS Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon SQS/Redis

## Relationships
* Fraud Analyst / Risk Manager -> Case API Controller: Interacts via HTTPS (Web UI) with OAuth2/OIDC authentication
* Case API Controller -> Case Business Logic: Invokes internal functions via TypeScript
* Case Business Logic -> AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Persists case states via SQL/TLS
* Case Business Logic -> Amazon SQS/Redis: Queues asynchronous outbox messages
* Audit & Immutable Ledger Publisher -> Secure Audit Archive: Publishes signed audit logs via gRPC/HTTPS
* Rule Feedback Publisher -> Fraud Scoring Engine: Submits rule adjustment flags via gRPC/HTTPS
* Card Masking / Tokenizer Integration Client -> Payment Card Network / Tokenization Vault: Ingests tokenized references via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
* Node.js & TypeScript: Enables rapid UI-driven feature iteration for fraud analysts
* AWS Fargate: Hosts containers cost-effectively with auto-scaling to respect the 25,000 EUR monthly budget
* AWS Aurora PostgreSQL & Amazon Redis: Provides structured data persistence and asynchronous message queuing
* Zod / Joi: Enforces strict JSON schema validation on API inputs to prevent injection attacks
* AWS Secrets Manager: Manages automated rotation of database credentials and OIDC secrets

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict PCI-DSS Level 1 data minimization by excluding raw PANs from the Node.js memory space. It also ensures 7-year auditability and fault-tolerant asynchronous logging tailored for a three-engineer team.

Audit & Compliance Ledger.analysis:
## Overview
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages analyst reviews.
- Operates under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year tamper-evident auditability constraint.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst / Risk Manager
- Compliance Officer / Internal Auditor
- Regulator / Card Scheme Investigator
- API Gateway (Nginx / AWS ALB)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Go with embedded ONNX Runtime)
- Case Management Service (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Audit & Compliance Ledger (Rust)
  - Ledger Ingestion Component
  - Cryptographic Sealer Component
  - Storage & Export Component
  - Compliance Query & Export Component
- Analytics Export Stream (Fluent Bit sidecar)
- Data Store (AWS Aurora PostgreSQL & Amazon Redis)
- Secure Audit Archive (Amazon S3 Object Lock)
- Identity Provider
- Payment Gateway / Processing Engine
- Payment Card Network / Tokenization Vault
- AWS KMS

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Processing Engine -> API Gateway: Submits authorization requests [HTTPS (TLS)]
- API Gateway -> Fraud Scoring Engine: Routes scoring requests [gRPC / HTTP/2]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Audit & Compliance Ledger: Sends decision payloads [gRPC via mTLS]
- Audit & Compliance Ledger -> Secure Audit Archive: Stores raw payloads and writes daily Merkle roots [HTTPS (TLS) / S3 API]
- Audit & Compliance Ledger -> AWS KMS: Signs Merkle root hashes [AWS KMS API]
- Compliance Officer / Regulator -> Audit & Compliance Ledger: Queries and exports audit bundles [HTTPS (TLS) via OAuth2/OIDC]
- Audit & Compliance Ledger -> AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Persists metadata and Merkle blocks [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol (TLS)]

## Technology Stack
- Rust: Chosen for the Audit & Compliance Ledger for memory safety and minimal operational overhead for a 3-person team.
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Stores immutable append-only ledgers and Merkle metadata.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: WORM storage for cost-effective 7-year raw payload retention.
- AWS KMS: Secures cryptographic non-repudiation via digital signing of Merkle tree roots.
- Go & Node.js: Utilized for high-performance scoring and case management containers.

## Rationale
- The architecture meets sub-50ms latency and strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget constraints through efficient Merkle tree batching and S3 offloading.
- It guarantees PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability without exceeding the operational capacity of a three-engineer team.

Analytics Export Stream.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for mid-size payment processors to detect and prevent fraud. It evaluates payment requests in real time and provides a case management interface for fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst / Risk Manager (User)
- Payment Gateway / Processing Engine, Identity Provider, Payment Card Network / Tokenization Vault, Secure Audit Archive (External Systems)
- API Gateway (Nginx / AWS ALB)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Java/Quarkus or Go with embedded ONNX Runtime)
- Case Management Service (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Audit & Compliance Ledger (Rust or Go with AWS KMS-backed signing)
- Analytics Export Stream (Rust/Go Local Anonymizer sidecar & AWS Kinesis Firehose Client)
- Data Store (AWS Aurora PostgreSQL & Amazon Redis)
- Data Lake (Amazon S3)

## Relationships
- Fraud Gateway -> API Gateway: Forwards authorization requests [HTTPS / gRPC]
- API Gateway -> Fraud Scoring Engine: Routes payment payloads [gRPC]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Data Store: Reads risk profiles and historical data [TLS / JDBC]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Audit & Compliance Ledger: Writes immutable decision logs [gRPC]
- Case Management Service -> Data Store: Reads and updates review cases [TLS / SQL]
- Analytics Export Stream -> Data Lake (Amazon S3): Batch uploads anonymized metrics and schema payloads [HTTPS / AWS SigV4]

## Technology Stack
- AWS (Cloud Provider, eu-west-1 region) for infrastructure deployment
- Java/Quarkus or Go with embedded ONNX Runtime for high-performance fraud scoring
- Node.js / TypeScript for case management services
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon Redis for transactional and cached data storage
- Rust/Go for local anonymization sidecar to ensure zero-allocation PII scrubbing
- Amazon S3 with AWS KMS customer-managed keys for secure data lake storage

## Rationale
This architecture uses high-performance microservices and in-memory caching to achieve decision latencies below 50 ms at P99 under 3,000 requests per second. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability through local PII scrubbing, cryptographic signing, and strict separation of analytics streams from live payment paths.

Data Store.analysis:
## Overview
[A secure, low-latency data storage layer built on AWS Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon ElastiCache Serverless Redis powers real-time payment fraud screening and case management.]

## Key Elements
* Feature Store: Amazon ElastiCache Serverless Redis cluster for high-velocity transaction features.
* Operational & Audit Database: AWS Aurora PostgreSQL Multi-AZ for case management and transaction history.
* Audit Archive Exporter: AWS Lambda function with Amazon EventBridge scheduling.
* Security Controls: AWS KMS Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs) and AWS Security Groups.
* External Storage: Amazon S3 Glacier Vault with Object Lock.

## Relationships
* Fraud Scoring Engine -> Feature Store: Fetches real-time transaction features via RESP / TLS 1.3.
* Case Management Service -> Operational & Audit Database: Persists analyst reviews via PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / TLS 1.3.
* Audit Archive Exporter -> Secure Audit Archive: Transfers immutable audit logs via HTTPS / TLS 1.3.

## Technology Stack
* Amazon ElastiCache Serverless Redis: Provides sub-millisecond feature reads to meet P99 latency targets.
* AWS Aurora PostgreSQL Multi-AZ: Ensures reliable relational storage for compliance and case management.
* AWS Lambda & Amazon EventBridge: Automates serverless log archiving with minimal operational overhead.
* Amazon S3 Glacier Vault: Implements tamper-evident, cost-effective 7-year audit retention.
* AWS KMS: Enforces column-level encryption and AES-256 data protection.

## Rationale
[This dual-engine storage architecture balances sub-50ms performance requirements with strict PCI-DSS compliance and a 7-year audit mandate. Furthermore, serverless components minimize operational toil for a three-engineer team while respecting the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]
